page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Doing lunch
title: Doing lunch
description:
Anna is determined to be friendly with her new colleagues and to make a good impression. Unfortunately, a slight misunderstanding leads her to make an embarrassing mistake.
This episode explores expressions you can use to introduce yourself and make small talk in the office.
phrases: Hello, I don't think we've met.

listening_challenge.question: What is Tom's job title at Tip Top Trading?
listening_challenge.answer:
What is Tom’s job title at Tip Top Trading?
Senior Account Manager.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Last week, Anna got the job of sales executive at Tip Top Trading, thanks to her quick-thinking in an office crisis. Today it's her first day in the office. How are you feeling now, Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Excited, but a bit worried. I really want to make a good first impression.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, you're going to need some phrases to introduce yourself politely, such as:
Why don't you start by saying hello to Tom Darcy, the Senior Account Manager?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yah, yah, no, yah, yah, OK, yah. I'll seal the deal, yah, no worries. OK, see ya mate, bye!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello, I don't think we've met.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You must be Tom. I'm Anna. I've just joined the team.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Uh huh.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Nice to meet you. Have you worked here long?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sorry, I'm quite busy right now – I've got a big deal just coming through. But let's get together sometime. Um... can you do lunch tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You want me to do lunch? Well, I'm not very -

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text:
Sorry, important client. Lunch tomorrow at 12.30 then?
(On the phone) Tom speaking. Yah! Frankie! So what's the latest, are we on?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, OK then.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Great Anna! You used some nice phrases to introduce yourself. It's a shame Tom thinks he's too important to do the same.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm sure he's just busy. But I'm a bit worried about tomorrow!
(The next day…)

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Good morning Paul!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Good morning Anna, are you OK?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Fine, the kitchen's through there, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Er, yes.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi, Denise!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: What are you doing?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Cooking lunch for Tom.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You what?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom asked me to have lunch ready for 12.30.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Did he indeed?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Er, Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hi Tom!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What are you doing?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Spring rolls, followed by crispy duck in black bean sauce.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No, I mean, why are you cooking?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, if I don't start now, it won't be ready for you by 12.30.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, you misunderstood me, Anna. When I said "Can you do lunch?" it didn't mean "Can you make lunch?" It meant "Are you available to come to lunch with me?" In a cafe or something.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Mmm... something smells good, but what's going on here?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Anna thinks it's her job to cook for people!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, no, I misunderstood!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna just got a bit confused.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, never mind, it looks tasty.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: There's enough for everyone if you want some.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I think that's a splendid idea, we can have an office picnic!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Mmm, that sauce looks delicious.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, it's my favourite.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, once again everything has worked out well for Anna! Before we go, a reminder of the phrases she used:
Just remember - if somebody says "Would you like to do lunch?" they're not usually expecting you to cook for them! Goodbye.
